dedupe_keys.name: ntsb carol investigations database and aviation accident data sets

description: The National Transportation Safety Board investigates every civil aviation accident in the United States and significant accidents in the other modes. CAROL (Case Analysis and Reporting Online) lets users search its investigations and safety recommendations across all transport modes. For aviation, the accident database holds civil aviation accidents and selected incidents from 1962 to the present in the United States, its territories and international waters, plus foreign investigations in which the NTSB took part; complete downloadable data sets are published for 1962 to 1981 (PRE1982.zip) and from 1982 to the present (avall.zip), with coding manuals and data definitions for each generation, a monthly accident list and a dashboard of US civil aviation accident statistics for 2008 to 2024. Data are free and public; an openICPSR copy is archived on Harvard Dataverse. Caveats: coding schemes change between generations, recent cases stay preliminary until the final report, and non-aviation modes cover only the major accidents the Board investigates. The data give event histories and probable causes for safety, fragility and resilience analyses across transport modes, and pair with FAA ASIAS incident data.
